name: Pan American
label: Kranky
lede: The guitarist from the band Kranky was founded to release went off on his own in 1997, and nearly three decades later he's still making Kranky records, now with a photo of his late mother on the cover.

eras.title: The band a label was built for
eras.text: Mark Nelson sang and played guitar in Labradford, a Richmond, Virginia trio whose slow, drifting debut was the reason Kranky existed at all. In 1997 he started a second project of his own.

years.h: Kranky starts in Chicago to release Labradford's Prazision LP
years.p: Joel Leoschke and Bruce Adams found Kranky in spring 1993 specifically to put out [[Labradford|7cf7ef41-9637-4bf2-ae99-d8d6611ccdc6]]'s debut. Mark Nelson's band is Kranky release number one.
years.xp: Labradford, with Nelson, Carter Brown and Robert Donne, went on to make six albums for Kranky between 1993 and 2001 and toured with [[Godspeed You! Black Emperor|3648db01-b29d-4ab9-835c-83f6a5068fe4]]. They never officially split, but they haven't released anything since Fixed::Context.

years.h: Mark Nelson starts recording as Pan American
years.p: While still in Labradford, Nelson begins a solo project of electronics, dub rhythms and guitar under the name Pan American, often styled Pan•American.

eras.title: Dub, drift and a little help from Low
eras.text: Pan American's first four albums all came out on Kranky, running alongside Labradford's last records. The second one brought in Chicago cornetist Rob Mazurek and two members of Low.

years.h: Pan American: Mark Nelson's self-titled Kranky debut
years.p: The first Pan American LP arrives on Kranky, five years after Labradford's debut on the same label.

years.h: Labradford launches its Festival of Drifting
years.p: Mark Nelson's band starts its own Festival of Drifting series, a home for the slow, spacious music Kranky had made its name on.

years.h: 360 Business/360 Bypass with Rob Mazurek and Low
years.p: Pan American's second album features cornetist [[Rob Mazurek|73c34525-f9c6-4c33-9abe-007748aaebe5]] and Low's [[Alan Sparhawk|36aa434c-6823-44b7-b5a6-53bde476c642]] and [[Mimi Parker|31e0783a-9c5d-4218-9f23-4b9427b111e7]], a rare meeting of Kranky's drone world and Duluth's slowcore.
Labradford releases its sixth album. The members later move away from Richmond, and Pan American becomes Mark Nelson's main outlet.

years.h: The River Made No Sound on Kranky
years.p: Mark Nelson's third Pan American album, his first after Labradford went quiet.
Pan American's fourth Kranky album closes the project's first run of records.

eras.title: Chicago, and a second player
eras.text: Mark Nelson made a detour to the Austrian label Mosz, came back to Kranky, and for the first time made Pan American a real duo with Chicago drummer and electronic musician Steven Hess.

years.p: The only Pan American studio album of the era not on Kranky, released by the Vienna label Mosz.

years.h: White Bird Release: Pan American back on Kranky
years.p: Mark Nelson returns to Kranky after five years away from the label.

years.h: Cloud Room, Glass Room: Steven Hess joins Pan American
years.p: On this Kranky album [[Steven Hess|f6e3c48b-fe51-42b0-b002-9d77da680442]] is a full member for the first time, turning Mark Nelson's solo project into a duo. Pitchfork reviewed it in April 2013.

eras.title: A son, a mother and a silver plane
eras.text: After six years away, Pan American came back with a run of records that got more personal, then opened up to collaborations with Kramer and guitarist Michael Grigoni. The latest, made in Chicago, is about parenthood, losing a parent and going home.

years.h: A Son: Pan American's first album in six years
years.p: Mark Nelson's Kranky return after Cloud Room, Glass Room.
Mark Nelson's ninth Pan American studio album.

years.h: Pan American and Kramer on Shimmy-Disc
years.p: Mark Nelson teams with [[Kramer|d898e082-70d1-4a86-ac8e-ecdf89892994]] for Reverberations of Non-Stop Traffic on Redding Road, released on Kramer's revived Shimmy-Disc label. A second Kramer collaboration follows in 2025.

years.h: New World, Lonely Ride with Michael Grigoni
years.p: Pan American and guitarist Michael Grigoni make a duo album for Kranky, the same year as Interior of an Edifice Under the Sea with Kramer.

years.big: A photo he never saw while she was alive
q: one I never saw when she was alive
years.h: Fly the Ocean in a Silver Plane: Mark Nelson's mother on the cover
years.p: Pan American's Kranky album is about journeys, parenthood and losing a parent. The cover shows Mark Nelson's mother, ready to board the silver plane of the title.
years.xp:
Nelson says the record is anchored by two songs about travel and coming home: Jo Stafford's You Belong to Me and Chuck Berry's Promised Land. He recorded it at home over several years on electric and rubber-bridge acoustic guitar, Ableton Live and a Digitone synth.

Mallory Linnehan of Chelsea Bridge added violin and vocals, recorded at the Not Not space in Chicago.
